chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them.
That a man was brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام who had been found beneath the bed of a woman in her house.
So he said: “Did you see anything other than that?” They said: “No.” He said: “Then take him to a dung heap and roll him upon it, back and belly, then let him go.”

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the Commander of the Faithful, referring to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.خَلُّوا سَبِيلَهُ: release him and let him go
key_terms.رَجُلٌ: a man involved in the reported incident
key_terms.فِرَاشِ: bed or bedding under which the man was found
key_terms.مَخْرُأَةٍ: a place of filth or dung heap
key_terms.هَلْ رَأَيْتُمْ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ: a question asking whether any act beyond the mere suspicious circumstance was actually witnessed

ai.seo_question: What did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام rule when a man was found under a woman’s bed without proof of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a case presented to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning a man found in a compromising situation in a woman’s house. Since no further act was witnessed, he did not impose the hadd punishment for zina, but instead ordered a humiliating disciplinary response and then his release.
